transcript: Yesterday I saw Tammy Faye on Broadway, a new musical following the titular televangelist and the rise and fall of the entertainment empire she grew with her husband Jim Baker. This did not strike me as the most riveting concept but I guess I've seen weirder concepts work wonderfully on stage. With leveled expectations, this production was perfectly fine but nothing special. The pacing was good, the design elements and the direction were fun, and the cast is doing a great job. Tammy is an interesting personality and Katie Brayben plays her quite well while delivering a unique and enjoyable vocal performance. But the score itself with music by Elton John is pretty forgettable. Also the straightforward, biographical structure of the story just feels a little tired here. I think the biggest shortcoming though is that the show is just not very funny. You'll definitely chuckle here and there but the laughs don't roll and overall the vibe of the show is not as buoyant as I think it needs to be. Although I found this pretty easy to sit through, I think for a musical comedy, it is somewhat lacking in the realm of music and comedy. With that, another playbill for my collection.
